WS7 Reviews real AI output

Editing an AI-Drafted Lesson: An Editorial QA Case Study

A real AI draft, every issue logged, and the clean final side by side.

An AI model was given a lesson brief, and its unedited draft was reviewed as a curriculum editor would: accuracy, alignment, accessibility, style consistency, bias and sources. The case study shows the redline, the issue log by category and severity, the revision cycle, the clean final and a print proofing pass. Every issue is one the draft really had.

Editorial QA · Copyediting · Accessibility review · Print proofingOpen WS7 →WS6 Representative sample

Measuring What the Unit Teaches: Assessment and Rubrics

Every item mapped to a standard, every wrong answer explained.

An end-of-unit assessment for Nature's Engineers: a blueprint, 22 items across selected-response, evidence-based and constructed-response formats, answer keys, distractor rationales, scoring rubrics and an item review checklist. It shows how each item measures the standard it claims, what each wrong answer reveals, and how teachers can read the results.

Item writing · Blueprints · Rubrics · AlignmentOpen WS6 →WS1 Representative sample

Nature's Engineers: A Grade 4 Knowledge-Building Unit

How do beavers, termites and coral change the places they live?

A Grade 4 unit built on a sequenced text set about animals that reshape their environments. Students build knowledge text by text, read closely, discuss, and write an explanatory piece that cites evidence. Includes the unit plan, knowledge progression, five fully written lessons, a culminating task with rubric, and a rights log for every text. All texts are original.
